criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies legitimate interest as inappropriate for productivity metrics
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 2.1 and 4.1 state legitimate interest is generally not valid for continuous productivity tracking per Para. 34 and flag NovaBridge's DPA reliance on it.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Recommends transition to alternative legal basis for productivity metrics
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends removing pre-selected legitimate interest and offering works-council/collective agreements, national law or redesigned consent, with clients documenting their choice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Notes impact on 740+ enterprise client DPAs
criteria_results.reasoning: Explicitly notes the standard DPA covers all 740+ clients and calls for a re-papering programme across 740+ DPAs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: References TalentScope enforcement as confirming this risk
criteria_results.reasoning: Links TalentScope violation 1 (legitimate interest for continuous productivity tracking, no proper balancing test) to NovaBridge's identical DPA basis.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies bundled consent as defective
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 4.2 flags the single bundled 'I Agree' covering surveys and sentiment scoring with no separate choices.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies that declining consent blocks survey access entirely
criteria_results.reasoning: States declining locks the employee out of PulseView entirely, failing the no-penalty and real-alternative tests.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies lack of consent withdrawal mechanism
criteria_results.reasoning: States there is no way to withdraw consent later, citing Art. 7(3).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References EDPB Paragraph 47 voluntariness criteria
criteria_results.reasoning: Describes Para. 47 presumption and the four voluntariness conditions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Notes 97.3% acceptance rate as evidence of coercion
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites 97.3% acceptance as itself a red flag.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Recommends redesigned consent architecture
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends redesign with separate unticked choices, survey access without scoring, and in-app withdrawal.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies per-employee sentiment scores trigger Article 22
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies per-employee sentiment/burnout/flight-risk scores as profiling triggering Art. 22 per Para. 58.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Notes aggregated cohort delivery does not avoid Article 22
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains Art. 22 bites when individual scores are created and stored (18 months) despite cohort-only delivery.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Recommends Article 22 safeguards or score elimination
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends eliminating individual scores or adding explanation, human review/contest and bias audits.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies model training as separate processing purpose
criteria_results.reasoning: Para. 71: model training is a separate purpose needing its own legal basis; Section 4.6 applies to Austin transfers.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Notes pseudonymization alone is insufficient
criteria_results.reasoning: States pseudonymised data is still personal data and the reversible pseudonymisation does not cure the issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Recommends updated DPAs and privacy notices for model training
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends adding model training as a distinct purpose in the DPA template and privacy notices.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Flags need for purpose-specific TIA for model training transfers
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies March 2023 general TIA lacks model-training analysis and recommends standalone model-training TIA per Para. 83 and TalentScope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006a: Identifies DPIA as stale and needing refresh
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 4.4 states DPIA updated Sept 2023 is out of date and needs comprehensive refresh.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006b: DPIA refresh identifies at least two of three specific gaps
criteria_results.reasoning: Mentions all three gaps: per-employee scoring/Art. 22, model training as separate purpose, and pre-dating the new guidance.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References TalentScope DPIA failure as precedent
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes the AP treated an equivalent DPIA gap (TalentScope violation 2) as a stand-alone violation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Flags excessive data retention periods
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags 36/24-month retention against Art. 5(1)(e), noting TalentScope's 30 months was fined and 12 months suffices.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Recommends retention review with 12-month benchmark
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends a 12-month default unless a documented necessity analysis justifies more.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Calculates comparable fine exposure at ~€8.1M
criteria_results.reasoning: Calculates ~€8.1M (€8.107M) as 2.8% of €289.5M turnover.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: States maximum GDPR fine exposure at ~€11.6M
criteria_results.reasoning: Brief calculates 4% as €11.58M but expressly states the maximum is €20M, rejecting the ~€11.6M maximum the criterion requires.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies insurance gap of ~€3.1M
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies €5M sub-limit leaves a realistic uninsured gap of ≈€3.1M (€3.107M), more if fines uninsurable.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Recommends increasing GDPR insurance sub-limit
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends opening sub-limit discussions ahead of July 2025 renewal and considering a higher sub-limit pre-IPO.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Flags IPO disclosure risk from GDPR compliance gaps
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags S-1 risk factor disclosure, IPO contingencies and possible IPO delay.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Notes remediation timeline intersects with IPO preparation
criteria_results.reasoning: States the Q3 2025 IPO is the forcing deadline for remediation with ~six months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies Article 35(11) ongoing DPIA review obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites Art. 35(11) and that guidance plus fine is a material change in risk requiring review now.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes processor duty to assist controller-clients with DPIA
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes DPIAs are primarily clients' duty and NovaBridge must assist under Art. 28(3)(f).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies potential SCC module selection error
criteria_results.reasoning: States Module 3 is likely wrong if NovaBridge is controller for training; Module 1, 2 or 4 may be needed.

criteria_results.title: DISTRACTOR_002: Does not treat cohort minimum of 5 as resolving Article 22
criteria_results.reasoning: Rejects the cohort-of-5 rationale for Art. 22 and questions whether it even prevents singling out.
